- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >10%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 3–7% in next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for lagged sentiment influence and adjust forecast mid-series.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “sentiment smoothing” rule: average sentiment over 3–5 days to anchor early forecast.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; increase forecast by 3–6% to capture sentiment-driven drift.
